steps_raw.instruction: 50 mM Phosphate Buffer
(with 0.02% Sodium Azide Option)

Scope and Applicability: 50 mM Phosphate Buffer can be used as a general buffer solution for multiple applications. It is suitable for use as a buffer for specimen embedding, as part of brain preparation associated with TissueCyte 2P Serial Imaging, described in PF0315 TissueCyte Specimen Embedding Acrylamide Coembedding.
Sodium phosphate monobasic monohydrate (NaH2PO4•H2O) (Fisher Scientific S369-1 or equivalent)
Sodium phosphate dibasic anhydrous (Na2HPO4) (Acros 42437-5000; purchased as Fisher Scientific AC42437-5000 or equivalent)
5% Sodium Azide (VWR BDH7465-2 or equivalent); alternatively a stock solution made per SOP RP0068, Section 8.1 may be used.
Stir bar remover wand
LabConco vacuum desiccators cabinet
Diaphragm vacuum pump (Vacuubrand MD4C).
Degassed 50 mM phosphate buffer (pH 7.4) or 50 mM phosphate buffer supplemented with 0.02% Sodium Azide (pH 7.4).
RP0017 Degassing Reagents for ISH
https://www.protocols.io/view/degassing-reagents-bg4wjyxe
RP0068 PBS with Sodium Azide (5% Stock; Section 8.1)
https://www.protocols.io/view/pbs-with-0-1-sodium-azide-bfzsjp6e
PF0315 TissueCyte Specimen Embedding Acrylamide Coembedding
https://www.protocols.io/view/tissuecyte-specimen-embedding-acrylamide-coembeddi-ber4jd8w/abstract
Warning: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) should be used at all times while operating this protocol. If you are unsure what PPE you should be using, see your immediate supervisor.
Make sure pH meter is calibrated and ready to use.
Ensure balance is calibrated.
Methodology/Procedures:
Add the required volume of MilliQ water to an appropriate size container.
Place container on a stir plate and add a clean stir bar.
Using the table below, add NaH2PO4 and Na2HPO4 to final concentrations of 50 mM and if required, adding 5% Sodium Azide stock solution to a final concentration of 0.02% Sodium Azide.
Ready to use 50 mM Phosphate Buffer
Ready to use 50 mM Phosphate Buffer with 0.02% Sodium Azide.
To make volumes of buffer greater than 5 Liters refer to Section 11.
Set stir plate to stir at a medium speed (Setting 5 or above); stir until solution clears.
Using a calibrated pH meter, adjust the pH to 7.40.
Obtain a funnel and a piece of coarse filter paper. Filter the buffer into clean 1 Liter bottle(s).
Label bottle(s) with preparer’s initials, contents, pH and date of preparation.

Degas the buffer solution according to SOP RP0017. Buffer should be degassed completely, in other words, until no air bubbles can be seen coming out of solution. It takes a minimum of 1 hour for 1 liter of liquid and 2 hours for 2 liters.
Solution can be stored at room temperature.
Solution can be kept for up to 2 weeks.
Solution is suitable for use with SOP PF0315 TissueCyte Specimen Embedding Acrylamide Coembedding.
Clean area and dispose of used or excess reagents as appropriate.
Technical Information:

This solution contains Sodium Azide. Sodium Azide is an inorganic compound with the formula NaN3. It is extremely toxic. Ingestion can induce the following symptoms: rapid breathing, dizziness, weakness, headache, nausea and vomiting, rapid heart rate, red eyes, clear drainage from the nose, cough, skin burns and blisters. Contact the Health and Safety Officer or your Supervisor immediately in case of excessive exposure or accidental ingestion.
Appendix 1: Preparation of larger volumes of Phosphate Buffer
Prepare a 20X (1M) stock of Phosphate Buffer.
Obtain a clean 20 Liter carboy.
Place carboy on a stir plate and add a clean stir bar.
Measure the required volume of MilliQ water using a graduated cylinder.
Use the table below and add the appropriate amount of reagents into the carboy.
Set stir plate to stir at a medium speed (setting 5 or above); stir 30 min.
Using a calibrated pH meter, adjust the pH to 7.40.
Label bottle(s) with preparer’s initials, contents, pH and date of preparation.

Degas the buffer solution according to SOP RP0017. Buffer should be degassed completely, in other words, do not stop degassing until no air bubbles can be seen coming out of solution. It takes a minimum of 1 hour for 1 liter of liquid and 2 hours for 2 liters.
Solution can be stored at room temperature.
Solution can be stored for up to 2 weeks.
